title: Four Floats, Ten Whirlpools, One Winner! 🌊
description:
Which float wins the river: Arrow, Leaf, Kite or Twin? Call it before they leave the start line!

Four identical floats start side by side at the top of a river and nobody steers them. The water is one velocity field: a steady current that runs faster mid-river and slower along the banks with a gentle meander, ten whirlpools that drift slowly and pull inward as they spin, and three rocks the flow has to split around. The thousands of streaks are tracers drawn from that same field, so the current you see is exactly the current the floats feel. Each float follows the local flow with a little inertia and can bump the others, the rocks and the banks. A float caught by a whirlpool circles until it is flung back out. The map on the left shows the whole course from the first frame, and the strip at the top keeps the running order. The first float across the finish line wins, and the freeze at the line measures the gaps in hundredths of a second. Then the race rewinds along the winner's path.
Start lanes, left to right: Arrow, Leaf, Twin, Kite. The lanes rotate between episodes.
Flow, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 1782), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Which float did you pick?
